# [CS054] Dependency Capability Escalation (supply-chain-capability-escalation)

A dependency's reachable code uses a capability the lock file does not approve.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Supply Chain & Provenance |
| **CWE** | [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html) |
| **OWASP** | A03:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

codex-cli caps lock records which privileged capabilities (exec, network, file system, environment, unsafe, cgo, plugins) each dependency uses from reachable code. An upgrade that suddenly starts running processes or opening connections is how compromised packages behave. Escalations to exec, cgo or plugins, or to both environment and network access, are Critical.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```text
// .codexsentinel.caps.json approves only CAP_FS_READ for github.com/acme/parser,
// but the new version calls os/exec.Command from code your program reaches.
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```text
// Review the dependency change; if it is expected, approve it:
//   codex-cli caps lock
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [supply-chain-capability-escalation]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    supply-chain-capability-escalation: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore supply-chain-capability-escalation -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** supply-chain-capability-escalation
```
